text.text: The WonderSwan was released in 1999 as Bandai's handheld gaming system developed with assistance from Gunpei Yokoi, the creator of the Game Boy. The system featured a low-cost design, long battery life, and a unique control layout that allowed games to be played in both horizontal and vertical orientations. Its library included many Japanese titles, including Final Fantasy games, Digimon titles, and various role-playing and puzzle games. The WonderSwan Color and SwanCrystal later improved the display while maintaining compatibility. Although it remained primarily a Japanese market product, the WonderSwan developed a strong library and became one of the more successful alternatives to Nintendo's handheld systems.
